title: Only Eyes for You
timelineLabel: Before Fionn's death; exact phase unplaced
summary: Felix and Reiner accompany Lynleit and Fionn on church visits. Reiner behaves; Felix keeps flirting with the nuns until Lynleit loses patience.
purpose: Build a recurring comic interruption around the church visits, with Reiner's restraint beside Felix's repeated lapses and Lynleit's mounting irritation.
known: Lynleit and Fionn visit churches with Felix and Reiner accompanying them.
Felix promises to behave; Lynleit reminds him that he made the same promise at the previous church.
Reiner holds the door, stays with Fionn, and tells Felix they are leaving.
Felix asks when the choir rehearses, suggests becoming a regular visitor, and keeps talking to a nun after being called away.
Lynleit catches Felix by his tie and raises a Bible, warning him: "Flirt with nuns one more time!"
Felix leans back with his hands raised and replies: "I only have eyes for you."

known.text: Felix turns a correction of his behaviour into an opportunity to address Lynleit as a romantic interest.

known: Lynleit rejects his interpretation. A nun asks for the Bible back; Lynleit returns it without striking him.

known.text: Their ready physical familiarity suggests that this argument occurs within an established closeness, rather than between a distant officer and subordinate.

known: Lynleit releases Felix's tie. Fionn and Reiner wait by the doors; Felix starts to look back toward the choir, but continues outside when Lynleit calls his name.
openQuestions: Where among the events before Fionn's death does the outburst occur, and which church is it?
What business brings Lynleit and Fionn to these churches?
continuityBefore: Felix and Reiner accompany Lynleit and Fionn on recurring church visits before Fionn's death. Reiner behaves appropriately; Felix repeatedly flirts with nuns despite attempts to restrain himself. Lynleit's irritation accumulates across those visits. Exact dates, churches, and the business of the visits are not fixed.
continuityAfter: The outburst is the payoff to Felix's repeated flirting during the visits, not a jealousy reveal. His fixation on Lynleit and later developing attachment to Sherie remain as established; this interlude does not set a milestone in either relationship.
prose: At the church door, Felix promised he would behave.
"You said that at the last one," Lynleit said.
"I meant it then, too."
Reiner held the door for Fionn. Lynleit went in after her father; Felix followed, adjusting his tie.
By the time they were ready to leave, the organ had fallen silent. Felix had not.

Lynleit found him beside a pew, holding the end of his blue tie out of the way while a nun gathered a stack of music books. Two more waited in the aisle. He had put on the helpful expression she knew rather too well.
"Do you rehearse every evening?" he asked.
"Tuesdays."
"I might become a regular."
"Felix."
He turned. "She was telling me when to come back."
"She was telling you when the choir rehearses."
"Yes. I was listening."
Reiner stood beside Fionn at the end of the aisle. He looked at Felix, then at the doors.
"We're leaving," Reiner said.
"One moment."
A loose sheet slipped from the stack. The nun caught it against her skirt. Felix reached to help, added something in a lower voice, and smiled.
Lynleit took hold of his tie.
"We are leaving."
"Already? I was just making friends."
He sat down abruptly as she drew him back toward the pew. A Bible lay on the seat beside his hand. Lynleit picked it up before he could sit on that too.
"You can make friends outside."
Felix glanced past her toward the aisle. She pulled the tie a little farther.
"Flirt with nuns one more time!"
The book was above her shoulder now. Felix leaned back against the pew and raised both hands.
"I only have eyes for you."
Nobody moved. The sister with the music books looked from him to Lynleit. Behind her, the other two had stopped rearranging their pages.
Lynleit could feel the heat climbing to her ears.
"That is not what I said."
"I thought it might help."
"How?"
His eyes went to the Bible.
"Has it?"
"Excuse me."
Lynleit turned. The nun had shifted the music books to one arm and was holding out her free hand.
"May I have that back?"
For a moment Lynleit looked at the offered hand without understanding. Then she lowered the Bible.
"Of course. I am sorry."
She placed it carefully on top of the music books. One corner had caught beneath her thumb; she smoothed it before letting go.
Felix cleared his throat.
"The other hand, too, if you can spare it."
She was still holding his tie. She released it.
"Outside."
Felix straightened the knot. "Together?"
Lynleit looked at him.
"Going," he said.
Felix caught the loose end of his tie before it snagged on the pew and followed her into the aisle. Fionn was waiting by the doors.
Reiner held the door for them. Felix made it halfway through, then glanced back toward the choir.
"Felix," Lynleit said.
This time he kept walking.

title: Sleepers above the River
summary: On an early morning walk, Kyrien notices motionless human figures suspended above the river. He takes a boat downstream to see how far they extend.
purpose: Kyrien follows an unexplained manifestation out of curiosity. The figures remain passive.
known: Kyrien walks alone through Vilen early in the morning and reaches the river.
Human figures hang without visible supports, their heads lowered and limbs loose. Most appear to be men in trench coats and hats.
Kyrien looks for cables and a crane but finds neither.
He privately calls the figures Sleepers and takes a rowing boat downstream.
The figures neither attack nor communicate nor visibly react to his attention.

known.text: Some figures would be difficult to notice from the street; their positions do not suggest a display arranged for Kyrien.

known: Kyrien continues downriver. The scene stops before his journey ends.
openQuestions: When does this encounter occur, and what happens after Kyrien continues downstream?
Are the figures human, and who can see them?
What, if anything, does their appearance foreshadow?
continuityBefore: The preceding events and story phase are undecided. This is a solitary walk, not an MSF assignment.
continuityAfter: The continuation and main-plot connection remain undecided. No connection to the Drowned Choir or river leviathan is established.
prose: The traffic light changed while Kyrien was still half a street away. By the time he reached the crossing it had gone red again. No cars had passed.

He waited with his hands in his jacket pockets. Across the road, a delivery van stood outside a shuttered shop, its rear doors open. There was nobody beside it. Most of the windows above the shops were dark, although daylight had begun to show between the roofs.
Was everyone still asleep?

He crossed when the light changed and took the street toward the river. His shoes sounded loud beneath the overhanging balconies. At the end of the street the wind reached him, colder than it had been among the buildings, and he pulled his collar up.

Steps led down to an exposed strip of bank beside a wooden pier. Water slapped against its posts. On the opposite side, the upper windows of a row of houses had caught the morning light; below them the bank remained in shadow. Kyrien stopped at the foot of the steps and looked along the water.
Something dark hung above it.
For a moment he took it for something farther away, attached to a building across the river. He moved a few paces sideways. The thing shifted against the roofs.
It was a man.

Kyrien tipped his head back. Thirty metres up, perhaps forty. A dark trench coat reached below the man's knees, and a hat hid most of his lowered head. His arms hung beside him. One foot was slightly lower than the other.
Kyrien looked above him.
No cable. He followed the empty air to either side, looking for the end of a crane, then turned to check the buildings behind the pier. Nothing nearby reached high enough.
When he looked back, the man was still there.
A gust lifted the bottom of the coat and let it fall. The body turned a little, too slowly for Kyrien to be sure at first. The hands stayed loose.

He went out onto the pier. Its boards shifted under his weight, and the change of angle showed him a pale strip between one sleeve and a glove. Or perhaps it was the hand itself. He couldn't make out the face.
Farther downriver, above the embankment, another man hung against the light sky.

This one was heavier. His coat was shorter, his hat broader. His head had dropped forward in the same way. Kyrien looked from one to the other, then found a third beyond a roof, where he had mistaken the dark shape for part of a chimney.
Were they asleep?
He stood with that possibility for a few seconds. From this distance he couldn't see anyone breathing. He couldn't see a rope around a neck either.
Sleepers, then. He needed some word for them.
The first had turned far enough to show its other shoulder. It had done nothing else. Kyrien walked to the end of the pier, watching for a change as he came closer. There wasn't one.

A small rowing boat was tied beside the lower landing. Two oars lay inside it. He looked downriver again. The farthest sleeper disappeared behind the corner of a building when he leaned to his left; from the road above, he doubted he would have noticed it at all.
He stepped into the boat, steadied himself against a post and untied the line. The hull knocked against the landing before he pushed it clear.
For a little while he watched the pier recede. Then he set the oars in their places and pulled toward the middle of the river. The blades made two broad disturbances in the otherwise quiet water.

There were gaps between the figures. Past the first bend he went long enough without seeing one that he turned to look back. The man over the embankment was still visible behind him. Ahead, a narrow coat hung above a stand of trees.
Kyrien counted five before he lost sight of the first.

They were at different heights. One was little higher than the nearby roof; another hung well above it, perhaps fifty metres from the water. A sleeve stirred. Farther off, the hem of a coat moved in the opposite direction as the wind changed.
He let the current carry the boat beneath the next one.

From directly below he could see the soles of two shoes, trouser cuffs and the hands hanging clear of the coat. One hand was open. The fingers of the other curled slightly inward. The head remained beyond the shoulders and the brim of the hat.
Kyrien rested the oars and watched.
The boat drifted on. He had to turn on the seat to keep looking up. A shoe moved against the sky as the whole figure swayed, then settled.
He faced downstream again and took up the oars. Beyond the next stretch of bank, another hat and pair of lowered shoulders came into view.

title: Ash in the Family House
summary: Before the crisis reaches her home directly, Lynleit clumsily chases a grey male cat named Ash, catches him, then cannot bring herself to expel him into the rain.
purpose: Lynleit catches Ash but lets him stay because it is raining.
known: The scene occurs in the early chapters, after danger has begun outside but before Lynleit's life starts to collapse.
The grey cat is male and is named Ash.
The family maintained an original house in Turon while Lynleit's mother was alive and Lynleit was in junior school.
After her mother's death, the family moved to a Vilen residence for Fionn's access to the capital. Lynleit accepted the move only after securing the third-floor study-bedroom.
The Vilen house is a three-floor family residence on a wooded hill above the river that flows toward the city center, with a small rear park and garden.

Lynleit values the thick vegetation and the sound of leaves and branches in the wind. She regards nearby flowing water as life energy and seeks its emotional grounding despite her childhood fear of drowning.
The garden-facing first floor contains glass-enclosed relaxation areas that preserve contact with nature through every season.
Lynleit personally chases Ash through the house, revealing a clumsier and more childish side of her than her public role usually permits.
Lynleit eventually catches Ash.
She cannot bring herself to expel him because rain is falling outside.
Ash decides to remain and becomes a permanent loiterer in the family home.
openQuestions: Who else in the household accepts or resists Ash's permanent presence?
continuityBefore: The first disappearances have begun outside Lynleit's private life, but the full crisis, Fionn's death, and the destruction of her family security remain ahead.
continuityAfter: Ash remains inside the house as a quiet domestic echo of the danger Lynleit cannot keep outside. Later losses can turn the once-comic chase into an omen whose meaning becomes clear only in retrospect.

known: Only Lynleit sees the hands clearly. They seize her most violently and drag her underwater.

The unit commanded by Captain Heyk is massacred by forces he cannot understand or explain.

title: Beyond the Cordon
summary: Hiyu enters the quarantined park to test his impossible suspicion that magic is involved in the disappearances. Yulia goes with him to prove the theory wrong and keep him alive.
purpose: Hiyu's theory takes him and Yulia into a danger neither understands.
known: Hiyu and Yulia are university students in their mid-twenties who study criminology.
Yulia is a classical ISTJ and the top student in their class, with meticulous command of detail and criminological protocol.
Hiyu is an ENTP whose personal investigations rely on intuitive threads, improvised methods, and rapid hypothesis generation.
Without knowing that magic exists, Hiyu suspects it is involved in the disappearances.
Yulia enters partly to prove him wrong and partly to prevent him from facing the danger alone.

What do they find, and how do they survive or escape?
What lasting evidence, injury, or change in their relationship follows the trespass?

continuityAfter: Their evidence connects two civilian students to the larger institutional response. Hiyu correctly suspects magic but still lacks any complete knowledge of it.

summary: After surviving the shared curse in Doom Has an Address, Lynleit and Kyrien begin a sexual relationship and develop private jokes and ordinary habits before her pregnancy and disappearance near the Arc 2 threshold.
purpose: Their sexual relationship develops after the curse has ended, alongside Lynleit's work and the closing pressures of Arc 1.
known: The park encounter after Doom is their first successful sexual act, not their first intercourse. Reciprocal exploration and intercourse follow as separate stages.
Several further encounters follow before Lynleit's pregnancy and disappearance.
Later encounters become lighter and more playful as intimacy acquires familiar habits.
Kyrien later initiates firmly, reversing their usual pattern and marking desire as his own chosen action.
One later encounter occurs in Lynleit's third-floor study-bedroom at the Director's House.
MSF duty and Lynleit's personal missions remain her priorities throughout the relationship.

known.text: The opening of Arc 2 lets the reader infer that Lynleit became pregnant near the boundary between the arcs, without a direct explanation or shown realization.

openQuestions: Which later encounter is the conception of their son?
What details at the opening of Arc 2 make the pregnancy inference clear without explaining or showing it directly?
How much time passes between Doom Has an Address, their later encounters, the beginning of the pregnancy, and Lynleit's disappearance?
continuityBefore: Fionn's death, the nonsexual hotel refuge, Doom's incomplete attempt, the later park encounter, and subsequent reciprocal intimacy precede the established sexual relationship. These are separate stages, not one compressed encounter.
continuityAfter: Pregnancy begins near the transition out of Arc 1. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from Kyrien and the wider world. Arc 2 reveals his existence to the reader; Kyrien's eventual discovery has no fixed timing. Intimacy is restored during Arc 2, ultimately leading to the conception and later birth of their daughter. That conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2. These are later continuity facts, not revelations in this Moment.

title: The Nameless Street
location: Vilen old town and an untraceable street
summary: During a casual walk after lunch with Felix, Lynleit enters a deserted labyrinthine street, follows a crying girl with a red balloon, sees a dead boy below a broken fence, and is pushed from the same ledge before waking on an ordinary city bench.
purpose: Lynleit returns with a memory of a dead boy that later resurfaces when she finds Fionn.
known: The Nameless Street is an urban myth in the old town of central Vilen.
Under unknown conditions, a lost visitor may enter it alone.
Its buildings and routes form a labyrinth that does not obey the surrounding city.
The warning attached to the myth is not to follow anyone encountered there, because those who do may never return to ordinary streets.
Days before Fionn's murder, Lynleit is walking with Felix after a work lunch when she abruptly finds herself alone, dizzy, unsteady, and suffering a severe headache.
A little girl carrying a red balloon appears, loses it, and runs away crying.
Lynleit catches the balloon by its thread and follows the girl's cries so she can return it.
The girl eventually stands beside a broken fence above an abrupt drop, looking down at the body of a dead boy.
Lynleit releases the balloon in shock. The girl smiles and pushes her from the ledge.
Before reaching the ground, Lynleit wakes on a bench in the ordinary city center while Felix fans her face with a piece of paper after her apparent faint.
Whether the street is a place, an illusion, or another kind of Holumn remains unresolved.
When Lynleit later sees Fionn's body below the hill at the family house, the memory of the boy stupefies her and gives Helena leverage to accuse her of pushing Fionn.

known.text: Felix does not explain why he accepts Lynleit's implausible account without laughing, leaving his response to be read through their long friendship.

openQuestions: What conditions admit a visitor to the Nameless Street, and why does it take Lynleit on this day?
Are the girl and boy inhabitants, repeated roles, former victims, or images produced by the street?
Does the fall release Lynleit, or does another interruption return her to the bench?
Does the street anticipate Fionn's death, draw from Lynleit's future, or leave a pattern that later events happen to reactivate?
What does Felix observe between Lynleit's last ordinary step and her collapse?
continuityBefore: Lynleit is already watching Helena study her family, but Fionn remains alive and the danger has not yet broken into an open accusation.
continuityAfter: Several days later Fionn is found below the hill at the Vilen family house. Lynleit's involuntary recognition of the dead boy gives Helena a true emotional reaction that can be assigned a false cause.

title: Father Mikhail Discovers the Breach
placementStatus: Middle-story placement confirmed, exact chapter unresolved
summary: Father Mikhail becomes the first authority to discover that Lynleit has shared forbidden knowledge of magic with outsiders. Kyrien corrects her attempt to limit the breach to himself by revealing that Felix and Reiner also know.
purpose: Mikhail's discovery forces Lynleit to answer for the witnesses and contributes to MSF's later Magi role.
known: Father Mikhail is the first authority to learn that Lynleit has disclosed forbidden knowledge of magic to outsiders.
Lynleit is unprepared for the discovery and promises to resolve the exposure on her own terms.
Mikhail asks whether Kyrien is the only witness, and Lynleit reassures him.
Kyrien immediately states that Felix and Reiner also know.
Mikhail responds by looking at Lynleit in judgment rather than escalating the confrontation openly.
Lynleit again promises to handle the problem in her own way.
Mikhail leaves her with the warning: 'What you do is none of my business, but don't be surprised if I'll be sent to clean up your mess.'
The encounter becomes an early cause of MSF's later transformation into a partly Magi private enterprise reporting to the Magiarchy and the Church.
After Mikhail leaves, Lynleit confronts Kyrien privately for exposing Felix and Reiner.
Kyrien does not apologize or retreat. Lynleit does not use her authority to punish him.

known.text: Their delay in stepping apart lets the reader register unwanted physical awareness inside the argument without turning the institutional conflict into a romantic scene.

known: Kyrien remains to help Lynleit address the breach after the argument.

known.text: Kyrien gives no reason for correcting Lynleit, leaving the reader to infer whether literal honesty, distrust of institutional half-truths, or another motive drives him.
Mikhail does not define his authority. His restraint and final warning imply that the Church may later send him back with powers he is not claiming in this conversation.

openQuestions: Where does the confrontation occur, and what evidence prevents Lynleit from denying the original disclosure?
What action does Lynleit mean by handling the problem in her own way?
What narrow authority would allow Mikhail to be sent back to clean up the breach?
What formal agreement later makes MSF accountable to both the Magiarchy and the Church while preserving its private ownership?
continuityBefore: Lynleit has already allowed Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner to operate with knowledge that ordinary MSF officers and outsiders are forbidden to possess.
continuityAfter: Lynleit must create an institutional place for people she refuses to suppress or surrender. Kyrien's refusal to preserve her convenient half-truth creates personal friction, but he remains involved in solving the exposure. The eventual answer changes MSF's mandate and places part of the private company inside the Magiarchal and Church order.

title: The Coat Fionn Left Behind
placementStatus: Middle of Arc 1 confirmed, exact scene unresolved
summary: Midway through Arc 1, after losing a blue suede jacket in the river and after Fionn's death, Lynleit learns that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wears with a garment sewn from material called the hide of leviathan.
purpose: Lynleit discovers Fionn's concealed gift and learns that she cannot command its form.
known: Lynleit loses a fitted blue suede jacket during the Drowned Choir attack and later complains about the loss because she liked it.
After Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wears.
The discovery occurs in the middle of Arc 1.
The replacement is sewn from material called the hide of leviathan.
The coat can shield its user from minor magically induced damage and phenomena.
Wearing the coat is not enough to activate its protection. Lynleit must cover the threatened part of her body or remove the garment and place or throw it over someone who needs protection.
The coat chooses its own form. It may appear as a coat, scarf, an imitation of Lynleit's lost blue jacket, or another piece of clothing.
Lynleit cannot command the change, which creates occasional practical and comic problems.
openQuestions: When did Fionn replace the original coat, and how did he do it without Lynleit noticing?
How does Lynleit discover the substitution after his death?
What does hide of leviathan mean, and is it connected to the river phenomenon recorded as HI-004?
What counts as minor magically induced damage, and what limits the coat's protection?
Why does the coat choose forms autonomously, and can it refuse the form Lynleit needs?
continuityBefore: Lynleit loses the blue suede jacket during the river operation. Fionn dies without explaining the protective garment he had placed in her wardrobe.
continuityAfter: The inherited coat becomes part of Lynleit's equipment. Its changing forms can preserve the silhouette of the lost jacket, but its protection remains deliberate rather than automatic.

title: Because There's a Battle to Be Fought
summary: Lynleit asks Kyrien why he continues to help her and risk his life when no reward awaits him. He answers immediately: "Because there's a battle to be fought."
purpose: Lynleit wants to spare Kyrien needless danger. He considers the fight sufficient reason to go.
known: Lynleit is bewildered by Kyrien's willingness to keep helping her and entering danger when no reward has been promised.
She does not want to place him in danger without necessity.
Kyrien answers bluntly and without hesitation: "Because there's a battle to be fought."
For Kyrien, the existence of a battle is itself a reason to enter it.
The impulse belongs to the same childish competitive streak that makes him want to win every game.

known.text: Kyrien does not say that he is fighting for Lynleit, leaving the reader to judge how much of his persistence is self-directed and how much attachment has entered a motive he still describes as combat.
His need to prove his worth may be directed toward his own standards, the memory of his father, or both.

openQuestions: Which operation or immediate danger prompts Lynleit to ask the question?
How does Lynleit respond to an answer that removes her from Kyrien's stated reason for staying?
Does Kyrien understand at this point that attachment has become part of the battle he keeps choosing?
continuityBefore: Kyrien has repeatedly accepted danger beside Lynleit, but rescue, coercion, and operational necessity do not fully explain why he keeps returning.
continuityAfter: Lynleit can rely on Kyrien without mistaking his involvement for obedience or romance. His later free choice to remain after her authority fails confirms that the answer was not an excuse.

title: Terrors Inside the Academy
placementStatus: Arc 1 placement and concurrency confirmed, exact chapter sequence unresolved
summary: While Lynleit is dispatched to Cardiff, she answers Natalia's request by sending Kyrien into the Magi Academy as Myka's undercover helper. The danger exceeds Lynleit's estimate and forces Natalia to intervene personally.
purpose: Kyrien protects Myka until the escalating danger forces Natalia to intervene.
known: Myka encounters terrors inside the Magi Academy.
She relies on Natalia for rescue, advice, and support.
Natalia asks Lynleit to help Myka.
Natalia was Lynleit's favourite teacher during Lynleit's Magi Academy years.
Lynleit cannot intervene personally because the Magiarchy and Church have dispatched her to Cardiff to assist Father Mikhail.
Lynleit sends Kyrien into the Academy as a substitute undercover helper.
Lynleit understates the threat and expects the assignment to help Kyrien understand the Magi world.
Kyrien enters the operation as a non-Magus working inside a Magus institution.
The danger Kyrien and Myka encounter exceeds Lynleit's estimate.
Kyrien relies on conventional field skills and communications with Felix and Reiner to keep Myka safe.
Natalia is forced to intervene personally.
This is Myka's first exposure to Kyrien and MSF.
The experience contributes to Myka's later decision to join MSF after graduation.
openQuestions: What terrors does Myka encounter, and why can the Academy not resolve them through its own hierarchy?
What cover, objective, and practical access allow Kyrien to operate inside the Academy?
How does Kyrien communicate with Felix and Reiner without exposing the operation?
Which event forces Natalia to intervene personally?
How are the Academy crisis and the Cardiff venture divided across their parallel chapters?
continuityBefore: Myka already relies on Natalia for ordinary academic advice and personal reassurance. Natalia asks her former favourite student Lynleit for help shortly before Lynleit leaves for Cardiff.
continuityAfter: Surviving the Academy crisis contributes to the knowledge and strength with which Myka later graduates at the top of her class. Her first experience with Kyrien and MSF gives her a personal reason to join the agency later.

title: Father Mikhail's Foreign Venture
placementStatus: Arc 1 placement and concurrency confirmed, chapter sequence unresolved
summary: Father Mikhail travels to Cardiff on special-envoy duty and is drawn into a life-and-death operation against several Magi threats. Lynleit is later sent abroad to assist him, without MSF or its conventional arsenal.
purpose: Mikhail and Lynleit complete their missions while disagreeing over their methods.
known: Father Mikhail travels to Cardiff to perform special-envoy duties for the Church.
The assignment develops into a life-and-death ordeal.
Mikhail faces several Magi threats alone before assistance reaches him.
He survives and defeats some of those threats, establishing him as a formidable Church warrior.
The venture reveals more of Mikhail's past, personality, and capabilities.
The Magiarchy and Church later request Lynleit's assistance in Cardiff.
Because Lynleit is abroad, she cannot rely on MSF or its conventional arsenal and must depend on her training as a Magus.
Lynleit and Mikhail continue to cooperate, fulfil their missions, and protect one another.
Their methods of solving the crisis are morally incompatible, and the rift between them grows during the operation.
Consequences from Cardiff later enter the main story in Narvea.
The Academy crisis unfolds in Narvea during Lynleit's Cardiff dispatch, dividing her responsibilities between a mission she must perform herself and a danger she has delegated to Kyrien.
openQuestions: What special-envoy duty brings Mikhail to Cardiff, and which event turns it into a life-and-death operation?
Which Magi threats does Mikhail face, and what Church techniques let him survive them alone?
What part of Mikhail's past is exposed by the operation?
Which specific method divides Lynleit and Mikhail morally while still requiring them to protect one another?
What consequence follows them from Cardiff into Narvea?
How many Chapters belong to the side story, and where do they alternate with the Academy operation?
continuityBefore: Mikhail already serves as a special envoy and has confronted Lynleit over forbidden knowledge. Natalia asks Lynleit to help Myka shortly before the foreign dispatch removes Lynleit from Narvea.
continuityAfter: Lynleit and Mikhail return from a successful but morally divisive cooperation. The Academy crisis has meanwhile forced Kyrien, Myka, Felix, Reiner, and Natalia into their first shared operation.

title: Myka Enters MSF
summary: After surviving the Academy crisis and graduating at the top of her class, Myka is recruited by MSF as a strong Magus.
purpose: Myka joins the agency she first encountered during the Academy crisis.
known: Myka survives the dangers she encounters inside the Magi Academy.
She graduates at the top of her class.
MSF later recruits her as a strong Magus.
openQuestions: Does Kyrien personally recruit Myka after becoming interim director?
Which Academy disciplines make Myka a strong Magus, and what can she not yet do despite graduating first?
How does her earlier undercover contact with Kyrien affect their later working relationship?
What role does Natalia play in deciding whether Myka should join MSF?
continuityBefore: Myka's Academy ordeal forces her to apply knowledge under danger and brings Kyrien into her life as an undercover helper.
continuityAfter: Myka enters the post-Spill agency as a trained Magus while Kyrien directs it without magecraft of his own.

title: The Unresolved Assassination
location: The hillside grounds of the Vilen family house
summary: Fionn is found dead below the hill at the Vilen family house after several incompatible agendas converge without one actor controlling the whole outcome. Helena knowingly opens one part of the path, then uses his death and Lynleit's stunned response to seize MSF and frame her.
purpose: Fionn's death connects the hidden conflict to Helena's visible takeover. The unresolved conspiracy contains several motives, partial knowledge, and accidental cooperation, with no single clean chain of command.
known: Fionn is successfully assassinated.
His body is found below the hill at the Vilen family house, but whether the fall kills him, follows another attack, or is staged remains unresolved.
Lynleit's recent memory of the dead boy on the Nameless Street stupefies her when she sees Fionn below the hill.
Helena assigns a false meaning to Lynleit's genuine shock and accuses her of pushing Fionn.
His death creates the opening Helena uses to take control of MSF.
Helena frames Lynleit for the assassination and directs a hunt for her arrest.
Helena knowingly enables one part of the pressure against Fionn without understanding everything that follows.
No single participant controls the complete assassination outcome.
Several incompatible agendas accidentally cooperate to produce Fionn's death.
The broader conflict already includes pressure from criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors.
The unresolved issue is how each participant's intended outcome and partial action converge into the assassination.
openQuestions: What outcome do the criminal Magi seek around Fionn?
What separate outcome does a rival foreign Magiarchate seek?
What separate outcome does a church faction seek?
Which actions accidentally cooperate even though their authors do not share one objective?
Did one faction covertly or illegally infiltrate another and use its people or resources without authorization?
Does any participant's apparent affiliation conceal who truly directed them?
Which door does Helena knowingly open, what does she expect to happen, and what follows beyond her knowledge?
Does the fall kill Fionn, conceal another cause of death, or stage the physical evidence used against Lynleit?
continuityBefore: Manufactured political strife isolates Fionn and divides his attention while the Spill develops. Days earlier, the Nameless Street gives Lynleit an unexplained memory of a boy lying dead below a fall.
continuityAfter: Helena converts the vacancy into control of MSF, makes Lynleit the official suspect, and directs a hunt for her arrest while the true authorship remains hidden.

title: Doom Has an Address
placementStatus: Later part of Arc 1 second half; exact placement unresolved
location: Several locations, ending in a private room
summary: Lynleit and Kyrien survive an identity-bound curse after an incomplete attempt at intimacy. Lynleit will not explain what she tried, and Kyrien does not know why they recovered.
purpose: The curse ends before Lynleit can use its treatment to explain away her continued interest in Kyrien.
known: Lynleit and Kyrien consciously destroy the same Holumn together.
Destroying the Holumn completes its mechanism and transfers its terminal condition to the people responsible for its death.
Their joint action leaves one curse distributed across two identities rather than creating two separate curses.
Both weaken, sleep ceases to restore them, minor injuries heal slowly, and ordinary exertion becomes difficult. Lynleit's magecraft also grows exhausting.
Suppressing the condition in either person fails because the remaining attachment reconstructs it in the other.
The traditional solution requires one of them to die first, collapsing the relation and releasing the survivor.
Lynleit refuses the fatal solution and consults other Magi, Magiarchal records, prohibited theurgy, Natalia, and Father Mikhail.

Natalia explains the shared attachment with two names on paper. She introduces the ego hypothesis and quotes Jung, using her failed decision diary, her departure from the Academy, and worry over Myka to distinguish descriptions of identity from changes in lived decisions.
Father Mikhail independently confirms that conversion, marriage, war, parenthood, confession, and other identity-changing experiences have disrupted related curses.
Mikhail tells Lynleit that sex could produce the necessary discontinuity only if a sufficient reciprocal attachment already exists.
Lynleit does not tell Kyrien about the proposed method and gradually begins treating their relationship as a possible procedure.
With the prognosis reduced to days, Lynleit attempts to initiate an encounter while behaving with unusual hostility and embarrassment.
The attempt does not fully cross the boundary between them, but the curse begins weakening the following morning and is later gone.

known.text: Lynleit's unread pages and repeated denials suggest that she remains interested in Kyrien after the curse is gone.

known: Kyrien knows Lynleit tried to sleep with him, refused to explain why, and became hostile whenever he mentioned the evening.
Kyrien suspects the attempt and their recovery are connected, but Lynleit withholds the proposed treatment.
The incomplete attempt and its aftermath change both identities enough to break the curse's recognition.
Lynleit answers Natalia's questions, jokes about her old marking, offers to approve her research, and keeps the diagram. Natalia acknowledges what she cannot measure and does not promise a cure.

Mikhail names Inanna, describes the lineage's three-thousand-year association with the Cult, and invokes ancestral covenants and the political importance of intimacy. Lynleit objects to his use of her family history.

known.text: Lynleit's repeated handling of her cup, formal defence, and threat of a canonically permissible reprisal suggest that his mock praise has struck personally.

known: Mikhail calls her response an observation rather than a diagnosis and says that physical intimacy is only a possible treatment, not a guaranteed cure.

known.text: Mikhail leaving Lynleit's averted gaze unremarked suggests a moment of restraint when his teasing reaches something personally difficult.

openQuestions: What identity, appearance, and prior incident history belong to the Holumn before Lynleit and Kyrien destroy it?
What operation places them in position to destroy it together?
Which Magi first identify the traditional one-death solution, and how much of the prognosis becomes known outside the four people in this scene?
What happens during the incomplete attempt?
What lasting effects, if any, remain after the curse collapses?
Where in the later second half of Arc 1 does this subplot fit relative to the unresolved main-plot chronology?
continuityBefore: Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge have already occurred. Kyrien has chosen to remain without Lynleit's former power to compel him. Doom is a later subplot in the second half of Arc 1, not a fixed immediate prelude to her disappearance.
continuityAfter: Months later, the park encounter is their first successful sexual act, specifically oral intimacy, not intercourse. Reciprocal exploration, first intercourse, an established sexual life, and pregnancy remain distinct later stages. The son is revealed only in Arc 2.
